p: a certain man named Ananias: Luke shows by contrary examples how great a sin hypocrisy is, especially in those who under a false pretence and cloak of zeal seem to shine and be of great importance in the Church.
kept back part of the price: Craftily took away.
filled thine heart: Fully possessed.

to lie to the Holy Ghost: For when they had appointed that farm or possession for the Church, they were foolish to keep away a part of the price, as though they were dealing with men, and not with God, and therefore he says afterwards that they tempted God.
conceived this thing in thine heart: By this is meant an advised and purposeful deceit, and the fault of the man in listening to the devil's suggestions.

tempt the Spirit of the Lord: Look how often men do things with an evil conscience; and so they pronounce sentence against themselves, and as much as in them lies, they provoke God to anger, as they do this on purpose, in order to test whether he is just and almighty or not.
door: Are at hand.
And great fear came upon all: The Lord by his marvellous power bridles some so that they may not hurt the Church: others he keeps in awe and fear of him: and others he draws unto himself.
magnified them: Highly praised them.
Then the high priest rose up: The more that the Church increases, the more the rage os Satan increases, and therefore they proceed from threats to imprisonment.

sect of the Sadducees: The word which is used here is "heresy", which signifies a choice, and so is taken for a right form of learning, or faction, or study and course of life, which the Latins call a sect: at first this word was used indifferently, but at length it came to be used only in reference to evil, whereupon came the name of "heretic" which is taken for one that goes astray from sound and wholesome doctrine in such a way that he thinks lightly of the judgment of God and his Church, and continues in his opinion, and breaks the peace of the Church.
But the angel of the Lord: Angels are made servants of the servants of God.
Go: God therefore delivers his own, so that they may more vigorously provoke his enemies.
words of this life: Words by which the way unto life is shown.
And when they heard that: God mocks his enemies attempts from above.
Then came one and told them: The more openly that Christ's power shows itself, the more the madness of his enemies who conspire against him increases.
Then went the captain with the: Tyrants who do not fear God are forced to fear his servants.
Saying: It is the characteristic of tyrants to set down their own commandments as right and proper, be they ever so wicked.
to bring this man's blood upon: Make us guilty of murdering that man whom yet they will not condescend to name.
Then Peter and the other apostles: We should obey man only in so far that in obeying him we also obey God.
The God of our fathers raised: Christ is appointed and indeed declared Prince and preserver of his Church, in spite of his enemies.
And we are his witnesses of: It is not sufficient for us that there is a proper goal, but we must also according to our calling go forward until we come to it.

were cut to the heart: This shows that they were in a most vehement rage, and tremendously disquieted in mind, for it is a borrowed kind of speech taken from those who are harshly cut in pieces with a saw.
Then stood there up one in: Christ finds defenders of his cause, even in the very company of his enemies, as often as he thinks necessary.
For before these days rose up: In matters of religion we must take good heed that we attempt nothing under a pretence of zeal to which we have not been called.
boasting himself to be somebody: To be of same fame.

Refrain from these men: He dissuades his fellows from murdering the apostles, neither does he think it good to refer the matter to the Roman magistrate, for the Jews could endure nothing worse than to have the tyranny of the Romans confirmed.
men: If it is counterfeit and devised.
And they departed from the presence: The apostles, accustomed to suffer and bear words, are eventually accustomed to bearing stripes, and yet in such a way that by means of them they become stronger.
temple: Both publicly and privately.
